local.h: Unhoused artist Peace Prophet's watercolors prized
local.b: Peace Prophet, a 71-year-old unhoused Chicago artist, paints watercolors collected across the city, some collectors owning hundreds.
more: She has lived on the streets since 2000 and turns down offers of housing help, accepting only payment for her work.

local.h: Denver weighs what to do with empty offices
local.b: About 38% of downtown Denver's offices sit vacant.
more: The city faces hard choices about converting or tearing down old office buildings without repeating urban renewal mistakes.

more: The walk took in four parks named for Black historical figures, including Madam C.J. Walker.

local.h: Malibu delays PCH speed camera fines to November
local.b: Malibu pushed its Pacific Coast Highway speed camera program to November, starting with a 60-day warning phase for drivers going 11+ mph over the limit.
more: A September test recorded about 100,000 speeding violations in under 10 days.
Since 2010, more than 60 people have died in collisions on this stretch of PCH.

local.h: How to get free mulch for your yard
local.b: Southern California residents can get free mulch through city programs or services like ChipDrop, which connects arborists with gardeners.
more: Los Angeles offers free mulch piles, while Orange County provides scheduled pickups.

local.h: LA mayoral rivals agree homeless agency must go
local.b: At a South LA forum, Karen Bass and Nithya Raman both backed leaving the Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority.
more: They split sharply on housing density and short-term rental rules ahead of the 2028 Olympics.

local.h: Could the billionaire tax reach everyone?
local.b: LAist fact-checked opponents' claim that Proposition 40 is a 'Trojan horse' for taxes on regular Californians.
more: Legal experts say lawmakers could make some amendments, but the tax's constitutional language limits how far it could expand.

local.h: Sixth person dies after falling ill in NYPD custody
local.b: Reginald Newkirk, 54, of Brooklyn died Sunday at Kings County Hospital, at least the sixth person this year to die after a medical crisis in NYPD custody.
more: He was arrested Friday for drug possession, hospitalized and cleared, then had another medical emergency Saturday afternoon.
Public defenders have called for independent Civilian Complaint Review Board investigations of every death in police custody.

local.h: NY prison system staffing crisis drives workers away
local.b: New York's prison system has a 56% vacancy rate among corrections workers.
more: New officer training is up 40%, but more than 250 of 660 newly trained officers resigned within a year.
The state spent over $1 billion deploying the National Guard after about 2,000 guards were fired following a 2025 wildcat strike.

local.h: NJ reports first West Nile Virus death of the year
local.b: New Jersey reported its first West Nile Virus death of 2026, a South Jersey resident over 60.
more: As of Thursday the state had confirmed 26 cases, 19 with neurological illness, already above last year's total of 23.

local.h: Banned books and Winnie the Pooh in NYC libraries
local.b: City library branches have a busy October, including banned-book events and NYPL celebrations of Winnie the Pooh's 100th birthday.
more: Queens Public Library and Penguin Random House are holding a banned book giveaway at the Hunters Point branch.

goodnews.h: Banned books and Pooh at NYC libraries
goodnews.b: NYC libraries mark Banned Books Week this October, with Queens Public Library offering free banned titles.
more: NYPL is celebrating Winnie the Pooh's centennial with movies, readings and crafts across the boroughs.

local.h: Up to 500 French schools to close Monday
local.b: The education minister said up to 500 schools will be fully or partly closed Monday because of protests by teenage pupils.
more: Protests disrupted more than 730 schools on Friday, and organisers have urged new rallies.
